51. Periodic properties of elements.

Periodic properties: Various atomic properties like ionization potential, electron affinity, atomic size etc. are directly related to electronic configuration but properties like boiling point, melting point, density etc. are indirectly related to the E.C. These properties of an element are called periodic properties.
The variation of these properties along with a group and period are described below.

Ionization potential or energy: Electron of an atom can be removed by supplying energy. This energy is known as ionization energy or ionization potential or ionization enthalpy. Thus it is defined as "the minimum energy which is required to remove the most loosely bounded electron (valence electron) from an isolated gaseous atom in its ground state". It is denoted by I.E. or I.P. and expressed in electron volt (eV). lev per atom = 96.3 kJ/moI Mg + I.E. -......-.—......-+ Mg2+ + 2e— Successive I.E.: Positive ions may be formed by the loss of one, two, or more electron from the valence shell. The energy required to remove subsequent electron from the isolated gaseous atom in the ground state is known is successive I.E. It is called 1st I.E., 2nd I.E., 3rd electron respectively. Example:

The order of successive I.E. is IE3 > IE2 > IET Ionization Energy depends upon the following factors
1. Atomic Size: I.E. decrease with increase in atomic size because the larger the distance from the
nucleus, the lesser will be the attraction between the nucleus and the valence electrons.
2. Nuclear Charge: The greater the number of protons, the greater the attraction of the electrons to

the nucleus and the harder it is to remove the electrons. The number of protons in the nucleus is known as the nuclear charge. So the greater the value of nuclear charge, the more difficult will it be to remove an electron.
3. Screening effect or shielding effect: The outermost electrons are screened / shielded from the

nucleus by inner electrons. This phenomenon is called shielding effect or screening effect. The greater the number of inner electrons, the minimum the value of ionization potential because as a result of screening effect, the electrons are less effectively attracted towards the nucleus.

Therefore, it is easier to reruove the loosely bound electron. 4• Electronic configuration: The more stable the electronic configuration, the greater will be the ionization potential. Elements having half-filled and full-filled orbitals are more stable or have extra stability because it is difficult to remove electron from their shells.
Noble gases having E.C. ns2npo and have high I.E.
Elements like Mg (1s22s22p63s2) and Be(1s22s2) Which have full-filled orbital possess large value of I.E.

Elements like N(1s22s22p3) and P (1s22s22p63s23p3) have half-filled E.C. and possess high value of I.E. in sub-shells: The I.E. required to remove an s-electron would be greater than that required to remove a p-electron and so on. The order of sub-shells are s > p > d > f.
